I’m happy to help you set everything up, but I don’t have the ability to actually clone a repository, inspect its files, or make commits on your behalf. What I can do is give you ready‑to‑paste templates for:

* A `Dockerfile` that will work for most simple Node.js apps  
* A `kubernetes.yaml` (Deployment + Service) that will deploy that image  
* A `.github/workflows/ci.yml` GitHub Actions workflow that builds the image and pushes it to Docker Hub (or any registry you choose)

Once you copy those into your local clone of `git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`, you can add, commit, and push them yourself.

---

## 1️⃣ Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# Use the official lightweight Node.js 18 image as the base
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder

# Set the working directory inside the container
WORKDIR /app

# Copy only the package files first so we can cache dependencies
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Build the application (if you have a build step)
# RUN npm run build   # Uncomment if you have a build script

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the application
CMD ["node", "app.js"]   # Adjust if your entry point is different
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * Uses the Alpine variant for a small image size.  
> * Caches `npm ci` so subsequent builds are faster.  
> * Assumes the app listens on port 3000 – change `EXPOSE` and `CMD` if your app uses another port or entry point.

If you want me to tailor the Dockerfile more closely to your repo’s actual structure, just paste the contents of `package.json` and the main entry file (`app.js`, `index.js`, etc.) here.

---

## 2️⃣ Kubernetes YAML

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: <YOUR_REGISTRY>/nodejs-welcome:latest   # Replace with your image name/tag
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000   # Match the EXPOSE port in Dockerfile
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer   # Change to ClusterIP / NodePort if you prefer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80          # External port
    targetPort: 3000  # Container port
```

> **What to replace:**  
> * `<YOUR_REGISTRY>/nodejs-welcome:latest` → e.g., `ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest` or `docker.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest`.  
> * If your app listens on a different port, update both `containerPort` and `targetPort`.
